predecessors.note: The Date ancestral lands in northern Fukushima: Date City, Kawamata, Kōri and Kunimi (Masamune page), the Date district awarded to Isa Tomomune in 1189 (Date clan page). Cliopatria's Warring States Japan row draws all Japan as one shape; the daimyo domains and Edo han are internal units.

successors.note: 1871: the han system is abolished (Sendai Domain page); the Date clan page gives 1868 for the end of the Sendai Domain and 1871 for the end of rule.

capitals.name: Kurokawa Castle (Aizu)
capitals.note: 'Masamune made Kurokawa Castle in Aizu domain his base' in 1589 (Masamune page). The coordinates are the researcher's placement of Aizu-Wakamatsu.

capitals.name: Iwadeyama Castle
capitals.note: After the Kunohe Rebellion Masamune 'received Iwatesawa and rebuilt it as Iwadeyama Castle' and stayed 13 years (Masamune page). Coordinates are the researcher's placement.

capitals.name: Aoba Castle (Sendai)
capitals.note: 1601: Aoba Castle becomes the Date base; 1604: Masamune moved to the fishing village of Sendai with 52,000 vassals (Masamune page); the Date clan page gives 1601 for the seat. Coordinates are the researcher's placement.

correction.text: the Date ancestral lands: Date City, Kawamata, Kōri and Kunimi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a daimyo domain Cliopatria lacks (Warring States Japan draws all of Japan as one shape). 1584: Masamune succeeded Terumune; the page names the ancestral lands Date City, Kawamata, Kōri and Kunimi (forfeited in 1591). A 20 km circle (about 1,000 km2) stands for them; the pages do not list the Date holdings of 1584 (the Date clan page mentions a 'Yonezawa fief' of 300,000 koku).

correction.text: southern Mutsu: Fukushima Prefecture (Nakadōri, Aizu and Hamadōri)

keyframe_review.note: 1589: Kurokawa, Suriagehara and Sukagawa; 'sealed the Date clan's hegemony over southern Mutsu Province' (no count of provinces or koku). Fukushima Prefecture (58 cells, about 14,700 km2) stands for it; the Date clan page puts the Aizu seizure at Suriagehara in 1589 and gives 1590 for the Hideyoshi reduction.

1591: Masamune 'forfeited the Date ancestral lands' to Hideyoshi and, after the Kunohe Rebellion, received Iwatesawa, rebuilt as Iwadeyama Castle, where he stayed 13 years (Masamune page); the Yonezawa Domain page: Hideyoshi moved the Date to Iwadeyama and gave the Gamō Aizu. A 25 km circle at Iwadeyama (about 2,000 km2) is the researcher's reading; the page gives no koku.

1600: Ieyasu awarded Masamune the Sendai Domain after Shiroishi and Hasedo; promised one million koku, the formal rating was 625,000 koku (Sendai Domain page; 640,000 on the Masamune page; 620,000 on the Date clan page), Mutsu Province. Miyagi Prefecture (32 cells, about 8,100 km2) stands for it; the Date clan page has the Date receive 'twelve districts formerly held by the Uesugi'. The Uwajima cadet domain (100,000 koku in Iyo, created 1614) is not drawn.

The Date clan page instead has Hideyoshi oblige Masamune in 1590 to accept the Yonezawa fief (300,000 koku).
1591-1601: after the Kunohe Rebellion (13 March to 4 September 1591, Hideyoshi page) Masamune 'received Iwatesawa and rebuilt it as Iwadeyama Castle'; he stayed 13 years. The page gives no koku.

ledger.note: 1600: Ieyasu awarded Masamune the Sendai Domain (Masamune page, after Shiroishi and Hasedo against the Uesugi); established 1600 (Sendai Domain infobox). The Date clan page has the seat move to Sendai in 1601 and Masamune settle there in 1604 (Masamune page). The Tokugawa Shogunate row opens in October 1600; the page gives no month.
1600: Sendai Domain, 'Established: 1600' (infobox); 'Sendai Han'. Same house, same colour.
1601: Aoba Castle becomes the Date base of power (Masamune page); 1604 the move to Sendai village with 52,000 vassals.
1868: Sendai sponsored the Ōuetsu Reppan Dōmei after Sendai men killed the Chōshū officer Sera Shūzō in May 1868; 'the focal member of the Ōuetsu Reppan Dōmei against the Meiji Restoration'.
After the Boshin War 'Sendai's holdings were reduced' (Sendai Domain page, no date). The end of the contest is bridged to 1869, confidence 1.
1871: the domain 'was dissolved in 1871 under the abolition of the han system'; the Date clan page: 'ruled until 1871'.

wars.outcome: The Nihonmatsu surrendered in 1585 and Terumune was killed; Hitotoribashi (January 1586); Kōriyama (1588); Kurokawa and Suriagehara against the Ashina (1589); the Date held southern Mutsu.

wars.name: Siege of Shiroishi and Hasedo
wars.outcome: Masamune fought for the Tokugawa eastern army at Shiroishi and Hasedo during the Sekigahara campaign and was awarded the Sendai Domain.
wars.note: The Kagekatsu page gives the Uesugi defeat at the same sieges.

wars.name: Boshin War (Ōuetsu Reppan Dōmei)
wars.outcome: Sendai was the focal member of the northern coalition against the restoration; its holdings were reduced afterwards.
wars.note: The page gives no battles or end date.

certainty.note: The pages name castles, battles, towns and koku, not borders; the Date holdings are a circle at the start and the Fukushima and Miyagi prefectures later.

sources.title: Date Masamune
sources.note: 1584 succeeded Terumune; Ashina and Nihonmatsu wars 1584-1588; 1589 Kurokawa, Suriagehara and Sukagawa, hegemony over southern Mutsu; 1590 Odawara; 1591 forfeited the Date ancestral lands (Date City, Kawamata, Kori, Kunimi), received Iwatesawa (Iwadeyama) after the Kunohe Rebellion, stayed 13 years; 1600 Shiroishi and Hasedo, awarded the Sendai Domain, promised one million koku but 640,000; 1601 Aoba Castle; 1604 moved to Sendai; died 27 June 1636.

sources.title: Sendai Domain
sources.note: Established 1600 in Mutsu Province; Aoba Castle (Sendai Castle); 625,000 koku formal, promised one million; Date Masamune 1600-1636 and 13 daimyo; sponsor of the Ouetsu Reppan Domei 1868 after Sera Shuzo was killed in May 1868; holdings reduced after the Boshin War (no date); dissolved 1871.

sources.title: Date clan
sources.note: Home province Mutsu; Date district awarded to Isa Tomomune in 1189; 1589 Masamune seized the Aizu domain of the Ashina at Suriagehara, Kurokawa Castle; 1590 Hideyoshi obliged Masamune to accept the Yonezawa fief of 300,000 koku; 1600 the Date received twelve districts formerly held by the Uesugi and settled at Sendai, 620,000 koku; seat to Sendai 1601; Uwajima Domain 100,000 koku in Iyo created 1614; ruled until 1871.

sources.title: Yonezawa Domain
sources.note: 1591 Hideyoshi moved the Date clan to Iwadeyama and gave the Gamo clan Aizu.

sources.title: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
sources.note: Kunohe rebellion in Mutsu 13 March to 4 September 1591; Senboku uprising September 1590.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from five pages (Date Masamune, Sendai Domain, Date clan, Yonezawa Domain, Toyotomi Hideyoshi). A Sengoku daimyo house that continues as the Sendai han inside Cliopatria's single Warring States Japan row and then the Tokugawa shogunate row; identity runs 1584-1871 with a 1600 rename to Sendai Domain. Dated by the pages: the 1584 succession, the 1589 hegemony over southern Mutsu, the 1591 forfeiture and Iwadeyama move, the 1600 award, the 1601 Aoba Castle, 1868 and 1871. Page conflicts: the Date clan page has the Hideyoshi reduction in 1590 with the Yonezawa fief (300,000 koku), the Masamune page has 1591 forfeiture and the Iwatesawa grant, the Yonezawa Domain page 1591 Iwadeyama; the Sendai Domain page dates the domain 1600 (625,000 koku rated), the Date clan page 620,000 koku and the seat from 1601, the Masamune page 640,000 koku and 1604; the Date clan page says Masamune seized Aizu 'in Wakamatsu Province' (not a province). Not on the pages: the Date holdings before 1589 (Okitama, Nagai, the Yonezawa fief), the Sōma and Ashina land divisions, the 1869 reduction (no date), the 1614 Uwajima Domain in Iyo (100,000 koku), the Ichinoseki Domain (30,000 koku) and how the Sendai shape divides between Mutsu districts. The uesugi-clan dossier carries the Uesugi side of Shiroishi and Hasedo. The Toyotomi dossier carries the Tōhoku vassal tint from 1590. Counterparts: 'toyotomi-clan', 'tokugawa-shogunate', 'uesugi-clan' and 'empire-of-japan' exist; the others are clans named on the pages. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
